body: This doesn't like a large Git repository. What's the output of `( git status; time git status ) >/dev/null` ?

@romkatv 
```
real    0m0,008s
user    0m0,001s
sys     0m0,007s
```

Thanks!

So it takes 8 milliseconds for `git status` to compute the status of your Git repository. This makes sense given the size of the repository.

Starship being slow in this case isn't explained by the repository being large. It might be causing the slowdown but 1000x slower than `git status` is not the expected level of Starship performance as far as I know. Something went awry.

This says that libgit2 ate all CPU.

Can you clone libgit2, build `lg2` command line tool and time `lg2 status`? You'll first need to install `cmake`, `make` and `gcc`. Then run this:

```zsh
(
  emulate -L zsh -o err_return -o xtrace
  git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2.git ~/libgit2
  mkdir ~/libgit2/build
  cd ~/libgit2/build
  cmake                        \
    -DUSE_ICONV=OFF            \
    -DUSE_SSH=OFF              \
    -DUSE_HTTPS=OFF            \
    -DTHREADSAFE=ON            \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF    \
    -DUSE_BUNDLED_ZLIB=ON      \
    -DREGEX_BACKEND=builtin    \
    -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON        \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    ..
  make -j 20
)
```

When this command completes, you'll have `~/libgit2/build/examples/lg2`. This is sort of like `git` implemented on libgit2.

If `lg2 status` is fast, it means that either Rust bindings for libgit2 are slow, or Starship is using libgit2 suboptimally.

P.S.

I noticed that you are using Zsh. I have a personal interest in Zsh themes. If I may ask, why did you choose Starship? This won't help to resolve this issue, so feel free to not reply.

I see this behavior too.  For me, the performance varies with respect the number of changes in the git project, not the absolute size.  If i have a large git project with no changes in the working folder (clean git status), it's fast.  

I currently have a project with several thousand working directory changes (easy to achieve on a golang project with some vendor/ folder changes: a bunch of adds/deletes/renames).  git status is still quite fast, but starship takes several seconds.

It's definitely related to the git_status segment.  If I disable that, the problem goes away.  I also tried disabling all the counts (e.g. untracked_count.enabled and company).  That did not have an effect.  Performance was still very slow.
I'm seeing this too --it's a real show stopper

I'm seeing the same thing, cloning the WebKit official git repository `git clone git://git.webkit.org/WebKit-https.git WebKit` when entering the folder with starship is very slow.

After a build it's even A LOT slower but even `git status` then complains that `It took 3.81 seconds to enumerate untracked files`

I'd suggest that the git plugin should have an upper bound on it's execution time, having a working prompt without git branch name is better than a too slow to be usable prompt.
I saw this happening (git status being fast but starship being awfully slow) when having a 1GB untracked file. Deleting it fixed it.
can confirm this is due to large untracked file, deleting the files or disabling git_status plugin fixed the freeze for me.

also disabling `[git_status]` because it takes 4 seconds to complete but actual `git status` is 0.1
p.s. i don't have any untracked files

As a heads up, we've got a rewrite in the works that _substantially_ reduces time spent on git status.
After the release of #1057, this will be the next major milestone we'll be working on.

> we've got a rewrite in the works that _substantially_ reduces time spent on git status.

Can you share any information on how this speed up is achieved?
The main improvement on the git side of things is thanks to dropping libgit2 in favor of calling git directly.

> The main improvement on the git side of things is thanks to dropping libgit2 in favor of calling git directly.

Makes sense. Thanks for the info.

By the way, before ditching libgit2 in gitstatus I’ve also tried linking with git and calling its functions. This is really difficult and doesn’t pay off compared to forking into regular `git` and parsing the output. So it’s a good call for starship to invoke `git`.

I could also offer 10+ _minutes_ instead of seconds. After that my patience ran out :-). FWIW: directory containing git repository holding 10s of 1000s of files (but in subdirectories of the directory holding the .git directory).

I am going to close this issue since we have switched to calling git and parsing the output rather than using libgit2. This should both be faster for larger repos and will respect the `command_timeout` setting so starship won't hang while trying to get the status of the repo. While this isn't a perfect solution it should hopefully be sufficient until we can introduce a cache, async rendering, a daemon or some combination of all three.
